note: Recast from the original English description of Bourguignon & Roisin 2011 (new species; type locality Lake Kutubu, Southern Highlands Province, Papua New Guinea; the specific epithet from the Latin barba “beard”, referring to the setae covering the whole postmentum of the soldier). The type series includes 1 soldier holotype and paratypes from several colonies, with workers and nymphs; the species had previously been recorded as Parrhinotermes nr. queenslandicus. The measurement abbreviations of the original are expanded into full terms, in millimetres.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier has the postmentum covered with setae from the base through the upper part, which separates it from P. browni (postmentum setose on the upper half only) and from P. queenslandicus; the original key also separates them by “postmentum setose all over” versus “postmentum setose on the upper half only”. The alate and the soldier overlap in measurements with P. browni, so identification must rest on the postmental pilosity.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head with about 15 setae, posterior margin strongly rounded; frons and clypeus of medium size. Pronotum with about 100 setae. Antenna 17 segments. Measurements (mm; 6 individuals from the same colony): total body length 5.23—6.02; head length (to the apex of the clypeus) 1.06—1.10; head width (including the compound eyes) 1.24—1.27; pronotum length 0.44—0.65, width 0.85—0.98; forewing length 8.02—8.84; compound eye diameter 0.27—0.39.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head ellipsoidal, with about 50 small setae. Labrum long, reaching the apex of the mandibles, its apex forming a rounded brush. Postmentum setose from the base through the upper part. Antenna 13 segments. Mandibles straight, slightly curved apically, slightly serrate at the base. Measurements (mm; 30 individuals from 10 colonies): head length (to the apex of the clypeus) 1.11—1.33; head length (to the apex of the labrum) 1.51—1.75; maximum head width 0.95—1.12; pronotum width 0.53—0.65; right mandible length 0.66—0.79; maximum postmentum width 0.25—0.34, minimum width 0.16—0.22; hind tibia length 0.74—0.90. Distribution: common in the forests of southern New Guinea, with a single record from Indonesian Papua (62 km on the Nabire—Mapia road).
